claims.claim_text_normalized: The essential difference between anchor-based and anchor-free detection is how to define positive and negative training samples.
claims.evidence_quote_short: the essential difference between anchor-based and anchor-free detection is actually how to define positive and negative training samples

claims.claim_text_normalized: Adaptive Training Sample Selection (ATSS) automatically selects positive and negative samples based on object characteristics.
claims.evidence_quote_short: we propose an Adaptive Training Sample Selection (ATSS) to automatically select positive and negative samples according to statistical characteristics of object.

claims.claim_text_normalized: ATSS significantly improves the performance of both anchor-based and anchor-free detectors.
claims.evidence_quote_short: It significantly improves the performance of anchor-based and anchor-free detectors

claims.claim_text_normalized: Tiling multiple anchors per location on the image to detect objects is not necessary.
claims.evidence_quote_short: tiling multiple anchors per location on the image to detect objects is not necessary.

claims.claim_text_normalized: With ATSS, state-of-the-art detectors are improved to 50.7% AP without introducing any overhead.
claims.evidence_quote_short: With the newly introduced ATSS, we improve state-of-the-art detectors by a large margin to 50.7% AP without introducing any overhead.

claims.claim_text_normalized: The regression starting status (box or point) is an irrelevant difference between anchor-based and anchor-free detectors.
claims.evidence_quote_short: the regression starting status is an irrelevant difference rather than an essential difference.
